Senior review decision:  Keep the product teacher-first and student-support, keep the mathematical MVP narrow, and evaluate safety/precision before expanding arithmetic coverage. The proposal deliberately avoids full microservices and fully autonomous grading within the 15-week capstone.
Appendix A. MVP Support & Error Taxonomy

MathVision Kids is a 15-week AI-assisted grading and tutoring platform for Vietnamese primary education. It serves two connected workflows: teachers upload approximately 10-30 photographed student exercises for AI pre-grading and review, while students submit one exercise to receive step-aware hints and retry guidance.

The core MVP is intentionally narrow: one clearly bounded vertical addition or subtraction exercise per image, natural numbers only, with or without carry/borrow. The system reconstructs what the learner wrote, validates supported arithmetic deterministically, locates the earliest supported error, and routes uncertain cases to confirmation, retake, abstention, or teacher review.

The software uses a Java 21 Spring Boot 3 modular-monolith business core with Clean Architecture, React teacher web, React Native student mobile, PostgreSQL, MinIO/S3-compatible storage, and a separate Python FastAPI AI service. Celery/Redis is internal to the AI subsystem for asynchronous batch processing. The deterministic rule engine is the source of truth for supported arithmetic; an optional VLM is restricted to structured comparison and hint wording.

Success is measured by reproducible recognition/localization metrics, low false accusation/over-correction, observable batch processing, teacher approve/override evidence, and safe student feedback. Teacher authority remains final; the system does not perform fully autonomous official grading.

Project thesis:  MathVision Kids reduces repetitive teacher checking through confidence-aware batch pre-grading while helping students understand where to retry, without confusing AI uncertainty with a student mistake.

Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision, Educational Technology
Primary-school teachers and Vietnamese students in Grades 1-5

MathVision Kids is a teacher-first, student-support platform that processes class-sized batches of handwritten arithmetic for AI-assisted grading and also provides individual students with confidence-aware, step-level feedback.

Deliver and evaluate a working MVP for teacher batch grading and student self-correction in a constrained vertical-arithmetic domain, while preserving teacher authority over final grades and separating system uncertainty from student error.

For this five-person capstone, Nguyễn Văn Duy Mạnh combines Product Owner and Scrum Master accountabilities. Product decisions (value, priority, acceptance) and Scrum facilitation (cadence, impediments, transparency) are treated as separate responsibilities even though they are held by one person. Developers remain self-managing in how Sprint work is executed.
Product Owner: owns Product Goal, Product Backlog ordering, stakeholder decisions, and acceptance.
Scrum Master: facilitates Scrum events, removes/escalates impediments, and protects transparency and the Sprint cadence.
Developers: jointly own implementation quality and the usable Increment; technical ownership does not create hierarchy.
High-impact technical decisions are recorded as Architecture Decision Records (ADRs).
Supervisor reviews are planned at Weeks 5, 9, 13, and 15. Material changes to privacy, research validity, architecture, or mathematical scope require supervisor review.

Primary-school teachers repeatedly inspect handwritten arithmetic to reconstruct digits, check place-value alignment and carry/borrow, identify the first error, and assign or confirm a result. The workload becomes significant when 10-30 photographed submissions are checked in one session. Students, meanwhile, often receive only a correct/incorrect outcome and may not know where their work first diverged.

Camera-based math tools are strong at solving a photographed problem, but MathVision Kids focuses on evaluating the learner’s own handwritten work. This distinction creates a safety requirement: a recognition error by the system must not be presented as a student mistake.

Core problem:  How can the system reliably reconstruct handwritten vertical arithmetic, verify the earliest supported error, propose a grading result at class scale, and provide safe hints while explicitly managing uncertainty?

The problem will be validated in the first two weeks through at least five semi-structured interviews with primary teachers, tutors, or parents. The team will confirm the value of batch grading, acceptable workflow, review behavior, and hint style without expanding the frozen core domain.

Primary research question: Can a Hybrid recognition-and-rule pipeline with calibrated abstention support AI-assisted batch grading and earliest-error localization more safely than an OCR/rule baseline or a VLM-only baseline within the 15-week constraint?

The contribution is not a claim that OCR, VLMs, or automated grading are individually new. The contribution is the engineering and evaluation of a confidence-controlled, teacher-first workflow that combines deterministic arithmetic validation, asynchronous batch processing, human approval, and student tutoring.

Figure 2. System context and trust boundary.

Teachers use the web portal for assignment context, 10-30 image batch grading, review, and final approval. Students use the mobile app for one-exercise capture, confirmation, hint, and retry. Parents/schools are consent and governance stakeholders. External AI, when used, receives only minimum necessary context.

Spring Boot owns business state and authorization. FastAPI owns AI inference. Spring communicates with FastAPI only through versioned REST/OpenAPI contracts; Celery/Redis remains an internal implementation detail of the AI subsystem. This boundary allows AI components to change without destabilizing classroom/grading business logic.

paragraphs.text: AI-Assisted Handwritten Arithmetic Grading & Tutoringfor Vietnamese Primary Students
Math Vision Kids – AI-Assisted Handwritten Arithmetic Grading & Tutoring for Vietnamese Primary Students
Scrum master / Project Leader & contact details
The following signatures are required for approval of this document.

This document defines how the Math Vision Kids project will be organized, executed, monitored, and delivered. It consolidates the approved project scope, Scrum responsibilities, communication approach, development process, detailed execution schedule, planned effort/cost baseline, project risks, and deliverables. The plan is based on the Math Vision Kids Project Proposal.

Math Vision Kids is an AI-assisted platform for Vietnamese primary education with two connected workflows: teacher batch grading and student handwritten-arithmetic tutoring. The Core MVP supports one clearly bounded vertical addition or subtraction exercise per image, natural numbers with 1-6 digits, and carry/borrow operations for Grades 1-5. A teacher batch may contain 1-30 images (with 10-30 as the typical classroom batch), while the student flow processes one exercise at a time.

The system follows a hybrid safety-oriented pipeline: Computer Vision/OCR performs perception; a Structured Parser reconstructs rows, columns, place values, and carry/borrow state; a Deterministic Rule Engine is the mathematical source of truth; a Confidence Policy routes uncertain cases to confirmation, retake, or review; and the teacher retains final authority over grading decisions. Multiplication/division and other advanced mathematics remain outside the Core MVP.
